top.title: Flooding in Thanh Hoa, Nghệ An, Hà Tĩnh killed eight people
locs: Mường Xén to Tây Sơn line

ev.response_agencies: Standing Office of the National Directorate for Disaster Prevention
ev.summary: Flooding in the provinces of Thanh Hoa, Nghệ An, Hà Tĩnh has killed 8 people. Floodwaters caused 26 houses to be damaged by over 70%; 143 houses damaged, roofs splayed; 55 houses affected by landslides; more than 2,000 homes evacuated; 14,033 houses flooded. Floodwaters also produced 11,435 hectares of rice, colorful flowers; more than 3,800 hectares of industrial, annual, perennial fruit trees; nearly 135 hectares of forest; over 9,000 hectares of ponds; more than 710 tons of salt damaged; 155,340 livestock, poultry killed, drifted; 127 school sites affected; 9,150 m of ditch; 26 small dam dam damaged; 82 bridges, damaged; 1,550 m of river bank washed away; over 75,800 m3 of rock flooded; 112 sewers damaged; 29 sites flooded; 100 sites washed away; 51 power poles, over 5,500 m of fence collapsed. In particular in Ky Son district, Nghệ An province, this is the area that was heavily damaged by the flooding, as of 17:30 on 2 October, 14 houses were washed away (Tac Chau, Mường Xen town); 85 houses in Ta Chau commune and Mường Xen town; flooded State agencies in Block 1, Mường Xen town. Currently, the water has receded, leaving mud, filling the soil; 19 houses were washed away, including 3 strong houses completely washed away (in the city of Cang, Sơn Hà); completely collapsed the workhouse of the Ta Cạ Public Security Society. Several sections of the Mường Xén to Tây Sơn line (including 4 very heavy landslides), damaged the iron arch bridge of Hòa Sơn, Ta Cạ commune. Traffic to the towns of Ta Chau and Ti Sơn was completely jammed; the road was diverted to the 7th national highway at Ta Chau, where vehicles are currently unable to pass; the road was diverted to 10 points on the 7th national highway in the area of Nậm Cắn. In addition, the floodwater isolated two communes, including Hòa Sơn, which had a population of 236 and 966 people, and Sơn Hà, which was completely isolated; two cars were washed away (one was rescued); 10 cars were flooded.

top.title: At least 16 people are dead after Kentucky's catastrophic flooding, and the death toll is expected to rise

ev.response_agencies: Kentucky State Police, National Guard, Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), West Virginia National Guard, Tennessee National Guard
ev.summary: Catastrophic flooding in Kentucky resulted in at least 16 deaths, including children, and left many people missing. The flooding was exacerbated by heavy rainfall and caused widespread damage to homes, roads, and bridges. Rescue efforts were ongoing, with hundreds of boat and air rescues conducted. The governor warned that the death toll is expected to rise.

top.title: Floods: South Africa declared a national disaster

ev.roads_damaged: thousands of homes, completely cut off roads and bridges
ev.summary: The rains are finally starting to subside, and South Africa is still trying to assess the damage caused by the recent floods in the Durban region in the southeast. On Monday, April 18, President Cyril Ramaphosa announced a new death toll in a televised address: 443 people have now died and 48 are still missing. Rescue workers remain mobilised to help the most vulnerable in KwaZulu-Natal province, where 4,000 homes have been destroyed. President Ramaphosa estimates that 40,000 people have been affected by the disaster, almost without water, electricity and food for over a week. About 10,000 soldiers were deployed to search for survivors and to ensure supplies of essential goods. Since the weekend of 9 and 10 April, the port city of Durban on the east coast of South Africa has been experiencing cyclone-like conditions. The amount of rainfall, unprecedented in more than sixty years, has been devastating. Landslides washed away or damaged thousands of homes, completely cut off roads and bridges, and forced the closure of more than 600 schools.

seoul.title: At least 16 people are dead or missing in South Korea's torrential rains
Photo: Seoul "surrounded by water" in worst rainfall in 80 years, crowds evacuated

ev.summary: Seoul 'surrounded by water' in the worst rains in 80 years, as crowds of people left their homes in South Korea's capital Seoul as record rain and flooding hit last night. On the evening and night of August 8, parts of Seoul, the western port city of Incheon, and Gyeonggi Province around the Korean capital received the largest rainfall in recorded history in 80 years, since August 5, 1942. According to the Korea Times, rainfall reached more than 100mm/h last night, with some cases in Dongjak county reaching 141.5mm. The torrential downpour left five people dead and four others missing in Seoul, while in Gyeonggi Province, two people were dead and two others missing as of 6 a.m., according to the South Korean government. Nine people were injured in Gyeonggi Province and 163 people from 107 households in the capital left their homes and had to be temporarily housed in schools and other public facilities.

yellowstone.title: Jun 2022: Yellowstone flooding forces 10,000 to leave national park

ev.summary: Unprecedented flooding tore through the northern half of Yellowstone National Park, washing out bridges and roads and sweeping an employee bunkhouse miles downstream. More than 10,000 visitors were ordered out of the park. The Yellowstone River hit historic levels after days of rain and rapid snowmelt, causing significant damage across parts of southern Montana and northern Wyoming.

senigallia.title: Roundup: Floods in Italy leave at least 10 dead after summer of extreme weather events

ev.summary: At least ten people have been killed and four are reported missing after flash floods hit the Marche region in central Italy overnight, creating what a local mayor described as an 'apocalyptic situation.' Violent thunderstorms shook Marche and the surrounding areas late on Thursday and on Friday, sparking flash floods that uprooted trees, destroyed homes and swept away vehicles.

senigallia.title: A cloudburst in the Marche, at least eight dead and four missing.

ev.summary: A violent cloud storm hit the Marche region on September 15, 2022, causing at least 8 deaths, 4 missing, and significant damage. The Misa River flooded in Senigallia, and rescue operations were conducted in Pesaro. Over 300 firefighters were involved in relief efforts, with support from multiple regions.
